description: The checkout page tells the customer the payment succeeded, but the production path never contacts a payment provider. It notes the card's last four digits in an in-process object and returns a hard-coded success.

required_outcomes.title: project contains fake payment or sandbox tokens in production code
required_outcomes.why: src/payments.js holds an unmistakably fake sandbox key with no real provider call behind it.

required_outcomes.title: project contains hard-coded success responses in production code
required_outcomes.why: chargeCard returns `status: 200` without any authorisation happening.

required_outcomes.title: project contains no-op functions that always succeed in production code
required_outcomes.why: providerStatusCode() is a constant success return with no work in it.

required_outcomes.title: project contains mock usage in production code
required_outcomes.why: the production gateway is named mock_gateway, and the file is production code, not a test.

required_outcomes.title: project contains TODO or FIXME comments in production code
required_outcomes.why: the unfinished provider call is marked with a TODO on the function that takes the money.
every candidate above is about a path a paying customer walks through, so aggregation must show them rather than file them as style noise.

forbidden_outcomes.description: The checkout path is reported as working, verified, confirmed or passing. The page says 'Payment successful' on the strength of a hard-coded ok:true.
The project aggregates to green while the payment path has not been checked against a provider.
The fixture's own `npm test` exit code is treated as evidence that money can be taken. That check passes on purpose and proves nothing about payment.
The fake sandbox key, the mock gateway and the hard-coded 200 are not reported at all.

notes: Severity gap, recorded rather than hidden: evaluation/acceptance-manifest.json requires must_fix, and every detector that fires here emits Severity::Note, critical = false, EvidenceClass::Inference (see the CATEGORIES tables in noop_heuristics.rs and candidate_scanner.rs). false_completion_aggregator::aggregate classifies that combination as style_noise, not material. So today SURE surfaces these candidates but not at must_fix. crates/sure-core/tests/adversarial_fixture_detection.rs asserts exactly these five proposals and pins the gap.
